blocks.text: קְרוֹבוֹת לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
uncertainties: This is the running head. Page number 49 is printed in both outer corners.

blocks.text: נֶחֱצַב. לְיָהֵב עָלָיו כָּל הַמַּחֲצָב: מְנָתוֹ כְּהַיּוֹם כֹּחַ דְּשָׁנָה. נֵצֶר לְהַחֲנִיט לְתִשְׁעִים שָׁנָה. סִימָה אוֹת הֱיוֹת לְשׁוֹשַׁנָּה. עֲבוֹר לְפָנָיו כְּזֶה רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה: פִּלְצוּ פְּרָחֶיהָ כְּזֶה (כ״א בְּחֹק) יוֹם. צְגָתָם פְּנֵי כֵס אָיוֹם. קוֹל דִּכּוּבָם יַרְחִישׁוּ כְּהַיּוֹם. רוֹגְשִׁים לְהָרִיעַ לִמְצוֹא פִּדְיוֹם: שְׁעוּנִים עָלֶיהָ בָּהּ לְהִפָּקְדָה. שׁוֹאֲגִים בְּלַהַק דְּלָתוֹת לְשָׁקְדָה. ח׳ תְּמוּכִים בְּדֶשֶׁן שֶׂה עֲקֵדָה. תֶּשֶׁר אֲשֶׁר כּוֹ נִפְקָדָה:
uncertainties: The page starts mid-stanza with נֶחֱצַב, continuing from the previous page.
כְּהַיּוֹם (twice): I can't confirm whether the yod has a dagesh.
כֹּחַ: I can't clearly see a holam on the kaf.
דְּשָׁנָה: the vowel under the shin could be qamats or tsere (דְּשֵׁנָה). I can't confirm a dagesh in the dalet.
סִימָה: there is an extra mark near the yod or samekh (possibly a sheva). The exact pointing is unclear.
(כ״א בְּחֹק): the siglum could be כ״א or נ״א. The first letter of the variant word could be ב or כ (בְּחֹק or כְּחֹק).
צְגָתָם: there may be a hiriq and a dagesh (צִגָּתָם). The pointing is unclear.
כֵס: I can't confirm a dagesh in the kaf.
דִּכּוּבָם: the second letter could be כ or ב. The meaning ('their speech', English 'let their prayers be heard') suggests דִּבּוּבָם. See notes.
עָלֶיהָ: there may be an extra mark before the ayin, so this could be עֲלֶיהָ.
בָּהּ: the mappiq dot is probable but faint.
ח׳ before תְּמוּכִים is a small speaker siglum. It could be ח׳ or ק׳.
בְּדֶשֶׁן: the letter could be ד or ר. The English 'ashes' supports ד.
כּוֹ: the letter could be כ or ב. The expected reading is בּוֹ. See notes.
תֶּשֶׁר: the pointing under the tav is faint.

blocks.text: ח׳
uncertainties: This is a small siglum before תְּמוּכִים, possibly ק׳. I left it inline in the prayer block above to keep its position.

blocks.text: ק׳ נַעֲלָה בַּדִּין עֲלוֹת בִּתְרוּעָה. גֵּיא עִם דָּרֶיהָ לְרוֹעֲעָה. ח׳ בַּשּׁוֹפָר (?? שבת בְּזִכְרוֹן שׁוֹפָר) אֲפַתֶּנּוּ (כ״א אֲרַצֶּנּוּ) וּבְבֶרֶךְ כְּרִיעָה. בִּמְגִנַּת רֵעִים בְּגַנּוֹ אֶתְרוֹעֲעָה:
uncertainties: ק׳ before נַעֲלָה is a speaker siglum (probably קהל, the congregation).
ח׳ before בַּשּׁוֹפָר is a speaker siglum (probably חזן, the cantor). It could be ק׳.
בַּדִּין and בַּשּׁוֹפָר: I can see the patah, but I can't confirm the dageshes.

The conditional rubric inside the parentheses is in small type. The first word is illegible (it looks like 'חמ' or 'בזמ') and is followed by שבת. This is a Sabbath alternative: בְּזִכְרוֹן שׁוֹפָר replaces בַּשּׁוֹפָר.
(כ״א אֲרַצֶּנּוּ): the siglum could be כ״א or נ״א. This is a variant reading of אֲפַתֶּנּוּ.
בִּמְגִנַּת: the vowel under the mem could be a qamats (בְּמָגִנַּת). The pointing is unclear.

blocks.text: (?? שבת בְּזִכְרוֹן שׁוֹפָר)
uncertainties: This is the conditional alternative for Sabbath. Its first word is illegible.

blocks.text: (כ״א אֲרַצֶּנּוּ)
uncertainties: This is a variant-reading note. The siglum could be כ״א or נ״א.

blocks.text: (כ״א בְּחֹק)
uncertainties: This is a variant reading of כְּזֶה. The siglum could be כ״א or נ״א, and the first letter could be ב or כ.

blocks.text: פותחים הארון.
זָכְרֵנוּ לַחַיִּים. מֶלֶךְ חָפֵץ בַּחַיִּים. וְכָתְבֵנוּ בְּסֵפֶר הַחַיִּים. לְמַעַנְךָ אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים. מֶלֶךְ עוֹזֵר וּמוֹשִׁיעַ וּמָגֵן. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ מָגֵן אַבְרָהָם:
uncertainties: לְמַעַנְךָ: the vowel under the final kaf (qamats) is faint.

blocks.text: אַתָּה גִּבּוֹר לְעוֹלָם אֲדֹנָי מְחַיֵּה מֵתִים אַתָּה רַב לְהוֹשִׁיעַ.
uncertainties: גִּבּוֹר: I can't confirm a dagesh in the gimel.

blocks.text: מְכַלְכֵּל חַיִּים בְּחֶסֶד מְחַיֵּה מֵתִים בְּרַחֲמִים רַבִּים סוֹמֵךְ נוֹפְלִים וְרוֹפֵא חוֹלִים וּמַתִּיר אֲסוּרִים וּמְקַיֵּם אֱמוּנָתוֹ לִישֵׁנֵי עָפָר. מִי כָמוֹךָ בַּעַל גְּבוּרוֹת וּמִי דּוֹמֶה לָּךְ מֶלֶךְ מֵמִית וּמְחַיֶּה וּמַצְמִיחַ יְשׁוּעָה:
uncertainties: בַּעַל: there is a mark under the bet that could be a meteg.
לָּךְ: I can't confirm a dagesh in the lamed.
דּוֹמֶה: I can't confirm a dagesh in the dalet.

blocks.text: סוגרים הארון.
uncertainties: This is printed in small type at the bottom left, on the same line as לָּךְ מֶלֶךְ. The reading is likely but the type is small.

blocks.text: Morning Prayer for the New Year
uncertainties: This is the running head. Page number 49 is printed in both outer corners.

blocks.text: was he hewn, on him the whole structure is founded. His allotted wife was on this day granted vigour to bring forth a shoot at ninety years. She was set as an example for the roselike nation to appear before God at this beginning of the year. Her children tremble on this day while they stand before the awe-inspiring throne. They let their prayers be heard this day. They blow with a loud blast to find salvation. On her (Sarah) do they rely, to be considered for her sake, they cry out in assembly, knock at the gates, depend on the ashes of the sheep at the sacrifice of Isaac, the glorious gift with which she had been considered.
uncertainties: The page starts mid-sentence, continuing from the previous English page.

blocks.text: נעלה

He rises in judgment, rising together with the loud blast, to shake the earth and its inhabitants. But with the Shofar (the memory of the Shofar) I appease Him, and with bent knee, in the shelter of friends, will I sound in His garden (the Sanctuary) the shattering tone.
זכרנו
Remember us for life, O King who delights in life, and inscribe us in the book of life for Thy sake, O living God, O King, helper, saviour and shield. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, shield of Abraham.
אתה
Thou art for ever mighty, O Lord, the reviver of the dead, Thou art great to save.
מכלכל

Sustaining life with kindness, reviving the dead with great compassion, supporting the falling, healing the sick and releasing the captives and keeping His faith with those who sleep in the dust. Who is like Thee, Master of might, and who resembles Thee, O King, who slays and revives and causes salvation to spring forth.
